comparisons.peer_topic: Regulation of specific subsidiaries and activities
comparisons.peer_summary: Broker-dealer subsidiaries are regulated by the SEC, FINRA, and NYSE; the futures commission merchant subsidiary by the CFTC and NFA; insurance activities by state agencies; and consumer financial products by the CFPB. Certain subsidiaries are registered as swap dealers with the CFTC and conditionally as security-based swap dealers with the SEC.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs and Bank of America disclose that specific subsidiaries are registered with the CFTC as swap dealers. However, Goldman Sachs explicitly details the operational mandates of those rules (clearing, execution, real-time reporting, business conduct standards) in its primary swap dealer disclosure, whereas Bank of America's matching disclosure focuses on listing the various regulatory agencies overseeing its diverse subsidiaries (SEC, FINRA, NYSE, CFTC, state insurance, CFPB), with the CFTC swap dealer registration mentioned as one component of a broader regulatory map.

sentences.text: CFTC rules require registration of swap dealers, mandatory clearing and execution of interest rate and credit default swaps and real-time public reporting and adherence to business conduct standards for all in-scope swaps.
A number of these requirements, particularly those regarding recordkeeping and reporting, also apply to transactions that do not involve a registered swap dealer.
In addition, certain U.S. and foreign subsidiaries are also registered with the CFTC as swap dealers, and conditionally registered with the SEC as security-based swap dealers.

sentences.text: CFTC rules require registration of swap dealers, mandatory clearing and execution of interest rate and credit default swaps and real-time public reporting and adherence to business conduct standards for all in-scope swaps.
In the U.S., JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., J.P. Morgan Securities LLC and J.P. Morgan Securities plc are registered with the CFTC as "swap dealers".

As a result, these entities are subject to a comprehensive regulatory framework applicable to their swap or security-based swap activities, including capital requirements, rules requiring the collateralization of uncleared swaps and security-based swaps, rules regarding segregation of counterparty collateral, business conduct and documentation standards, rules requiring the central clearing of standardized over-the-counter ("OTC") derivatives, requirements that certain standardized OTC swaps be traded on regulated trading venues, record-keeping and reporting obligations, and anti-fraud and anti-manipulation requirements.

comparisons.peer_topic: Swap Dealer Registration and Capital/Margin Rules
comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm has registered as a swap dealer and conditionally registered as a security-based swap dealer, subject to margin and capital requirements established by prudential regulators or the CFTC/SEC, with potential compliance alternatives for non-U.S. entities.
comparisons.comparison: Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley both disclose CFTC rules requiring swap dealer registration and adherence to business conduct standards. A key difference is that Morgan Stanley provides specific details on capital and margin requirements, distinguishing between entities regulated by prudential regulators versus those subject to CFTC/SEC rules, and noting potential compliance alternatives for non-U.S. entities. Goldman Sachs' disclosure is broader, emphasizing real-time public reporting and the application of recordkeeping/reporting to non-dealer transactions.

sentences.text: CFTC rules require registration of swap dealers, mandatory clearing and execution of interest rate and credit default swaps and real-time public reporting and adherence to business conduct standards for all in-scope swaps.
A number of these requirements, particularly those regarding recordkeeping and reporting, also apply to transactions that do not involve a registered swap dealer.

CFTC and SEC rules require registration of swap dealers and security-based swap dealers, respectively, and impose numerous obligations on such registrants, including adherence to business conduct standards for all in-scope Swaps.

Swap dealers and security-based swap dealers regulated by a prudential regulator are subject to uncleared Swap margin requirements and minimum capital requirements established by the prudential regulators.

Swap dealers and security-based swap dealers not subject to regulation by a prudential regulator are subject to uncleared Swap margin requirements and minimum capital requirements established by the CFTC and SEC, respectively.
